summary: Lokesh Chandra (1927–2022) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the University of the Punjab, under Raghu Vira, and under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University. He served as Director of the International Academy of Indian Culture (~1963–2022).
Longlian (1909–2006) was a Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai Shi from circa 1941 to 1967.

Lore Sander (b. 1936) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1960–1967) and held positions including Curator at the Museum of Asian Art (1987) and lecturer at Free University of Berlin (1994).

Lori Meeks (b. 1976) works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University and Princeton University (PhD under Jacqueline I. Stone) and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Southern California in 2004.

Lorna Dewaraja (1929–2014) was a historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London, later serving as Associate Professor of History at the University of Peradeniya (~1960–1980) and faculty at the University of Colombo (~1980–1994).

Lothar Ledderose (b. 1942) works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He studied at Bonn, Heidelberg, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne. He was Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and Slade Professor at the University of Cambridge (~1991–1992).

Lothar von Falkenhausen (b. 1959) is a Sinologist and archaeologist. Educated at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard, he joined the University of California, Los Angeles, becoming Full Professor in 1993 and Associate Director from 2004 to 2011.

Louis Charles Casartelli (1852–1925) specialized in linguistics and Iranian studies. He studied at Ushaw College, University of London, and KU Leuven under Charles-Joseph de Harlez de Deulin. He taught at KU Leuven (1900–1903) and the University of Manchester (1903–1920).

Louis Deroy (1921–2003) was a Belgian scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven and the University of Paris, and pursued his academic career at the University of Liège, rising from chef de travaux in 1956 to ordinary professor in 1972.

Louis Dubeux (1798–1863) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics who studied under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy. He served at the Royal Danish Library, INALCO (Professor of Turkish, 1848–1849), and Collège de France (Professor of Hebrew, 1857–1862).

Louis Dumont (1911–1998) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Marcel Mauss, Walther Schubring, and Pierre Meile, graduating from the University of Paris. He taught at Oxford (1951–1955) and served as Directeur d'Études at EPHE and EHESS.

Louis Dupree (1925–1989) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He earned his B.A. from Harvard University and held posts at Pennsylvania State University, Princeton, UNC Chapel Hill, and Duke University.

Louis Duvau (1864–1903) was a French linguist. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, EPHE under Ferdinand de Saussure, and the University of Leipzig, and held a post at the École française de Rome (1887–1888).

Louis Finot (1864–1935) was a scholar of Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under Sylvain Lévi at EPHE, he directed the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1899–1904) and held chairs at EPHE (1917–1930) and the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Frédéric (1923–1996) was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Indology who completed his studies at the Sorbonne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Louis Gabaude (b. 1942) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient circa 1980 and circa 1990 to 2007.

Louis Gernet (1882–1962) was a French historian. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1902–1905) and held academic posts at the University of Algiers (~1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1948–1962).

Louis H. Gray (1875–1955) was a scholar of Iranian studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Princeton and Columbia under A. V. Williams Jackson, he was Associate Professor at Nebraska (1921–1926) and Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Columbia (1926–1944).

Louis Hambis (1906–1978) studied Central Asia and Sinology under Paul Pelliot at EPHE. He served as Director at EPHE, the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises (1959–1973), and Professor of Central Asian history at the Collège de France (1965–1977).

Louis Havet (1849–1925) was a French linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal and Abel Bergaigne. He served as Professor of Latin Philology at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.
